one_line: A human-consented mental-health intake and therapist-matching copilot.
what_it_does: Triages intake narratives, detects crisis language, matches therapists and recurring slots, and prepares a booking that requires explicit human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and server-side safety/consent checks make agent participation substantially more reliable than UI driving, especially for crisis interception and exact slot locking.
leverage_evidence: Two named WebMCP tools are described: triage_and_match_therapists and commit_intake_booking.
Packet claims authoritative backend crisis checks, slot locking, consent validation, and database commit.
Visible frame sheet shows an integrated intake application panel, but no legible tool name or returned result.
execution_rationale: The architecture and claimed workflow are coherent and the frame sheet shows a deliberate intake UI, but the submitted packet has no transcript and the frames do not visibly demonstrate an end-to-end completed booking.
execution_evidence: React/TypeScript frontend, Express backend, PostgreSQL, and Docker Compose are stated.
Frame sheet visibly shows TheraSync branding and a structured intake form with action controls.
No clear completed state, navigation, or legible output is visible in the reviewed frame sheet.
impact_rationale: Mental-health intake is a high-stakes, specific use case; crisis-aware triage and human-controlled booking credibly address safety and access needs.
impact_evidence: Crisis and self-harm language is claimed to stop routine scheduling and show emergency support options.
Booking requires human review and explicit approval.
creativity_rationale: The combination of WebMCP agent access, therapist matching, crisis gating, and human consent is an ambitious and thoughtful interaction model for a sensitive workflow.
creativity_evidence: Safety interception is integrated into the agent workflow rather than treated as a generic booking feature.
Two-phase slot locking and consent validation are part of the stated design.
usability_note: Structured form and human approval are promising; the reviewed frames do not establish full usability.
red_flags: High-stakes safety claims are primarily packet claims, not end-to-end demonstrated in the visible evidence.
standouts: Human consent and crisis interception are concrete safety boundaries.
advance_reason: Strong high-stakes use case and meaningful WebMCP leverage; end-to-end execution should be verified in Stage 2.

one_line: Behavioral coding fingerprints for programmer identity verification.
what_it_does: Analyzes prior and newly submitted source code to generate a coding fingerprint, similarity score, report, and supporting WebMCP analysis tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured analysis/report tools can improve repeatability and expose results to an agent, but the core identity analysis could plausibly be run through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes generated fingerprints, similarity scoring, and a downloadable report.
Devpost text references supporting WebMCP tools.
No video frame sheet was submitted, so tool invocation and state sharing are unverified.
execution_rationale: The described surface is coherent but evidence is thin: no video frames, demo status is unknown, and the packet text is sparse/duplicated.
execution_evidence: Packaging text lists final result, rating, report download, similarity score, fingerprint, radar chart, and WebMCP tools.
No submitted video evidence and demo_alive is unknown.
impact_rationale: Recruiting, authorship verification, and academic or team code provenance are credible needs, though behavioral fingerprints may have uncertain reliability.
impact_evidence: The stated problem is verifying whether a programmer wrote code beyond simple code similarity.
The product compares prior samples with new source code.
creativity_rationale: Behavioral coding style as a programmer identity fingerprint is a fresh concept with a memorable framing.
creativity_evidence: Coding DNA/fingerprint based on naming, structure, loops, formatting, comments, and complexity is the central novel angle.
usability_note: Reported scores and visualizations could be useful, but no runnable workflow evidence is supplied.
red_flags: No video frame sheet; demo status unknown.
Behavioral identity claims and false-positive handling are not evidenced.
advance_reason: Interesting concept but insufficient execution and WebMCP evidence for advancement.

one_line: A recorder and composer that turns workflows into portable agent skills.
what_it_does: Records browser workflows, has an LLM produce ordered SkillPlans and SKILL.md files, then runs multiple composed agents in parallel through a WebMCP dashboard.
leverage_rationale: The product is explicitly built around a page-published structured agent surface controlling shared composer state; general UI automation would be markedly less reliable for parallel plans and runs.
leverage_evidence: Packet claims 29 registered WebMCP tools across global, composer, and recorder surfaces.
Composer slots own separate goals, plans, runs, and live progress.
Recorder produces portable SKILL.md from screen frames and browser event timelines.
execution_rationale: The two-part product concept is coherent and ambitious, with a plausible recorder-to-plan-to-parallel-run workflow; frame evidence was not successfully available beyond packet claims.
execution_evidence: Detailed architecture distinguishes Recorder and Composer.
Claimed dispatch runs four agents in parallel against headless Chromium.
Live dashboard and portable output are described.
impact_rationale: Teams with repetitive browser workflows have a clear automation need, and reusable skills could reduce repeated manual work.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies recurring inbox, metrics, lead follow-up, report, and receipt workflows.
Portable SKILL.md output supports reuse beyond one run.
creativity_rationale: Combining screen recording, LLM workflow description, portable skills, and a 2x2 parallel agent composer is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Recorder and Composer form a distinctive end-to-end interaction model.
Parallel agent slots with independent plans and progress are a strong original synthesis.
usability_note: The split recorder/composer model is powerful but potentially complex; evidence does not establish polish.
red_flags: No transcript and reviewed visual evidence is incomplete; core claims need live verification.
standouts: Portable SKILL.md artifact and parallel composer are standout ideas.
advance_reason: Highest WebMCP centrality and unusually ambitious workflow automation concept; verify live execution.

one_line: A user-controlled memory boundary that agents must access through a visible WebMCP interface.
what_it_does: Lets users inspect, edit, permission, audit, and export memories while agents query and act through controlled page tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the trust boundary and capability interface, changing who controls memory access rather than merely automating an existing button.
leverage_evidence: Packet explicitly frames the website as memory, agent as consumer, browser as trust boundary.
Named surfaces include Memory Insights, Permissions, Audit export, and tool-call simulator.
The described model exposes only capabilities enabled by the user.
execution_rationale: The product model is coherent and extensive, with a visible dashboard and multiple control surfaces; end-to-end state transitions are not fully established by available evidence.
execution_evidence: Packet lists dashboard, canvas, simulator, permissions, audit export, and diagnostics pages.
Claims real memory state is inspectable and editable by the user.
Frame-sheet visual review was unavailable after provider rate limits.
impact_rationale: People using persistent AI assistants have a real privacy, control, and auditability problem; precise memory permissions and revocation directly address it.
impact_evidence: Product targets inspection, editing, selective revocation, and independent verification of AI memory.
User control over capabilities is central rather than incidental.
creativity_rationale: Inverting the usual agent-memory architecture so the website owns the user-controlled boundary is a strong and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The packet explicitly contrasts agent-owned APIs with a browser-mediated memory boundary.
Permissioned memory use, audit receipts, and a tool-call simulator deepen the concept.
usability_note: Inspection and permission controls fit the problem well; complexity of memory management remains to be validated.
red_flags: Privacy/security guarantees are claims requiring implementation verification.
standouts: Clear browser trust-boundary thesis and user-controlled memory surface.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP rationale and credible high-value problem; verify actual permission enforcement and audit behavior.

one_line: A WebMCP storefront where agents discover paid AI services but humans approve payment.
what_it_does: Publishes service discovery, input, pricing, market search, paid-request, and result tools; payment pauses for human wallet approval before service completion.
leverage_rationale: Typed discovery and a human-controlled payment checkpoint make agent commerce more reliable and safer than driving a storefront, while preserving human authorization.
leverage_evidence: Eight WebMCP tools are claimed for service listing, inputs, prices, search, request, and result checking.
Demo lifecycle claims HTTP 402 pause, visible activity, wallet approval, settlement, and result return.
Agent receives the completed JSON repair result directly.
execution_rationale: The claimed paid lifecycle is specific and coherent, including failure/approval boundaries and a concrete JSON repair demo; visual end-to-end confirmation is limited.
execution_evidence: Packet describes a real 0.005 USDC JSON Validate/Repair request.
Human approval, Base wallet connection, x402 settlement, and completed result are all specified.
Demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Agent-discoverable services and explicit payment consent address a real emerging commerce workflow for service providers and agent users.
impact_evidence: Service catalogue, pricing, request lifecycle, and result delivery form a concrete use case.
Human control prevents silent agent spending.
creativity_rationale: The combination of WebMCP discovery with x402 payment gating and agent-returned results is a timely, well-pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Payment intentionally stops at a human-controlled checkpoint rather than being fully automated.
Existing REST/OpenAPI/MCP service is reframed as a live storefront.
usability_note: Clear lifecycle and consent checkpoint; wallet/payment setup may add friction.
red_flags: Project existed before the challenge, although the WebMCP storefront addition appears challenge-relevant.
Payment and result claims need live verification.
advance_reason: Strong real payment flow and agent commerce leverage, with pre-existing origin noted separately.

one_line: A shared literature-review canvas for humans and browser agents.
what_it_does: Moves papers through review stages while agents search, inspect evidence, annotate, compare sources, create briefs, verify, and export on the same board.
leverage_rationale: Selection-aware typed tools, shared live state, receipts, and auditability materially change collaborative research compared with an agent clicking a UI or working in a separate chat.
leverage_evidence: Sixteen WebMCP tools are claimed across search, state, selection context, paper details, citations, notes, comparisons, artifacts, verification, and export.
Human and agent contributions appear on one board with author badges, tool-call receipts, and activity trail.
Workflow stages encode research state and completion.
execution_rationale: The staged workflow and evidence/audit model are coherent and complete for a literature-review canvas, though the packet lacks transcript and visible end-to-end proof is limited.
execution_evidence: Inbox, To Read, Reading, and Synthesized states are defined.
Packet claims same-board contributions and first-class artifacts.
Demo is reported alive; no gallery images or transcript supplied.
impact_rationale: Researchers have a clear collaboration and auditability problem, and shared evidence handling directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Product targets discovery, source verification, synthesis, and challenge of interpretations.
Cited conclusions and decision briefs preserve research accountability.
creativity_rationale: The shared research-room framing and selection-aware agent collaboration are a fresh synthesis pursued beyond simple paper search.
creativity_evidence: Research stages are represented as a living board rather than chat output.
Tool-call receipts and audit trails make agent research legible.
usability_note: The staged canvas fits research practice; density and workflow overhead should be tested.
red_flags: End-to-end search-to-cited-conclusion flow is not clearly demonstrated in the available packet evidence.
standouts: Strong shared-state and auditability framing for research.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP fit and credible research value; verify source handling and complete workflow live.

one_line: A basketball tactics board where an agent replans around a coach's locked decisions.
what_it_does: Creates, validates, animates, and repairs structured basketball plays while rereading live formation, timing, locks, and revisions after coach edits.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables the agent to read exact live board state and preserve human locks while making targeted repairs; screenshot-based UI automation would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes structured reads of formation, clock, actions, locks, and revision.
Agent retimes only unlocked actions after a coach changes the clock.
Seven deterministic validation checks and direct animation are claimed.
execution_rationale: The core two-turn workflow is unusually specific and internally coherent, with an error introduced by the coach and a constrained repair; frame count is small and no transcript exists.
execution_evidence: Claimed demo moves/saves locks, creates clock overflow, then repairs only unlocked pass and shot.
Final animation reportedly completes within two seconds and passes all seven checks.
Two submitted frame sheets are stated, but visual provider access was unavailable.
impact_rationale: Coaches and players have a real need to iterate on plays while preserving intentional decisions; the product directly supports that niche workflow.
impact_evidence: Specific basketball tactics-board audience and collaborative play-design workflow are described.
Live validation and animation make timing errors actionable.
creativity_rationale: The locked-decision, live-state repair interaction is a memorable application of WebMCP to tactical play design.
creativity_evidence: Agent must distinguish locked from unlocked actions and repair only the latter.
Clock-overflow failure and constrained retiming create a convincing interaction model.
usability_note: Direct manipulation plus animated validation is well matched to coaches; domain learning curve remains.
red_flags: The strongest execution claims are not independently legible in the unavailable frame review.
standouts: Human locks preserved through targeted agent repair.
advance_reason: Exceptional shared-state interaction and strong niche value; verify the repair sequence live.

one_line: A collaborative load-shifting sandbox that turns peak-energy alerts into approved reversible plans.
what_it_does: Lets operators lock critical loads, have an agent simulate candidate schedules, compare peak/cost/comfort/rebound risk, approve a diff, commit, and roll back.
leverage_rationale: The agent works against live constraints and staged visual state, with cancellability, explicit approval, deterministic simulation, commit, and rollback—far beyond generic UI clicking.
leverage_evidence: Dynamic WebMCP registration is based on UI state.
Agent reads demand event, locks, and flexible assets; candidate plans are simulated and staged.
Approval drawer, exact schedule diff, commit, rollback, and audit trail are claimed.
execution_rationale: The workflow includes safety constraints, candidate comparison, preview, approval, commit, and rollback, indicating strong scope coherence; direct visual verification was limited.
execution_evidence: Deterministic 15-minute integer watt-hour model and transparent heuristic solver are stated.
Critical loads never change and one-click rollback restores the prior schedule.
Demo reported alive; no transcript supplied.
impact_rationale: Facilities operators have a concrete operational and safety problem, and reducing peaks without disrupting critical equipment has credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets demand-response events and sudden price spikes.
Considers peak, cost, comfort, and rebound risk while protecting critical loads.
creativity_rationale: The visible, reversible human-agent load-planning loop is an ambitious and thoughtful application of WebMCP to energy operations.
creativity_evidence: Ghost preview plus exact schedule diff approval is a strong interaction pattern.
Rebound-risk comparison and rollback deepen the concept beyond a generic dashboard.
usability_note: Visual timeline constraints and approval drawer support safe operation; operational complexity needs testing.
red_flags: Safety and solver behavior are claims requiring live validation.
Video evidence could not be fully inspected due to vision-provider limits.
standouts: Safety-first staged planning with rollback and rebound-risk visibility.
advance_reason: High credible impact and transformative shared-state leverage; verify constraint enforcement and rollback.

one_line: A human-sealed reading desk for investigating uncertain handwriting with an agent.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect words, compare same-hand letters, check candidates, and suggest readings while humans accept, reject, or mark illegible; stale proposals are rejected.
leverage_rationale: Shared revision state and stale-proposal rejection make agent assistance safer and more precise than ordinary UI automation for evidence-sensitive transcription.
leverage_evidence: Eight native WebMCP tools are claimed.
STALE_REVISION prevents old proposals from overwriting newer human evidence.
Final export records decisions, evidence revisions, and a SHA-256 integrity hash.
execution_rationale: The synthetic ledger, evidence display, human sealing, stale protection, and integrity export form a coherent focused product; full visual end-to-end proof is not available.
execution_evidence: Three unclear words and same-hand comparison workflow are specified.
Only the human can accept, reject, or mark illegible.
HTML/CSS/JavaScript implementation is stated and demo is alive.
impact_rationale: Archivists, historians, genealogists, and transcription users face real uncertainty where preserving provenance matters; the product directly supports careful interpretation.
impact_evidence: Addresses faded, damaged, or missing handwriting in historical records.
Human-readable evidence and irreversible-looking mistakes are explicitly considered.
creativity_rationale: Human-sealed transcription with revision-aware agent proposals is a distinctive, appropriately constrained use of agent collaboration.
creativity_evidence: Stale protection and evidence revisions are central interaction mechanics.
Integrity-hashed export extends the concept into provenance.
usability_note: Evidence-first suggestions and explicit decision controls are well matched to uncertain reading.
red_flags: Synthetic evidence domain may not establish real archival robustness.
Integrity hash claim needs implementation verification.
standouts: STALE_REVISION is a concrete safety mechanism for human-agent collaboration.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-integrity interaction and clear niche value; verify stale rejection and export behavior.
